First off, I imagine that science and technology will be so advanced it would be futile to give a whole picture. Technologies which we simply cannot comprehend today, any more than a Medieval peasant could comprehend a computer, will be in regular use today. But I'll try and guess at some of the things we may have accomplished.

  • Longevity - I actually expect a cure for aging to be found this century, given the growing pace of research into the biology of aging and an increasing body of scientific evidence that aging can be reversed. Basically, every adult will have a body in its youthful prime. Lifetime will be indefinite, and deaths will be due to causes other than aging, like accidents. It's highly possible, I think likely, that there are people alive now, including young adults, who will still be alive in 3,000. The fact that the birth rate will be low will make up for it (the better off people are, the fewer children they tend to have, plus with indefinite lifespans will put off children for longer periods).

  • Computer technology will be so advanced, we may actually have attained the perfection of computer science, in which computers are as smart and fast and capable as physically possible. We will have created artificial superintelligence by then, which may well actually be running the world for us (though I'd expect we will have boosted our own intelligence by then too). The state of robotics will have advanced far beyond the hyper-intelligent robots of 20th-century science fiction.

  • Automation of everything - This I also expect to be completed this or next century, and to still prevail then. Basically, humans will no longer have to work to live. Robots and computers will take care of society's needs. With no need to work, we will devote our time to individual pursuits.

  • Humans and machines will have merged to the extent that the average human, by today's standards, is a hyper-intelligent super-powered cyborg. Although I suspect a fair amount, if not almost all of our time, will be spent in virtual reality. And I think we will have full-immersion virtual reality that is fully capable of creating highly detailed and perfectly realistic computerized worlds.

  • We will be able to manipulate the genes of living things. We will regularly tamper with the genes of babies before birth, creating "designer babies". And pregnancy will have been replaced by artificial wombs. The technology for this will probably be available in the mid-21st century.

  • I'm not sure about our power sources in this time, but I think we will be technologically capable of building a Dyson sphere at this point, if we so need it.

  • Space travel will be a regular thing. We will be fully settled on other worlds, having colonized our solar system, and will also have undersea cities.

  • We will be able to manipulate matter to a massive extent. Think the replicators of Star Trek, as well as teleportation.

  • If it's physically possible, we will have cracked faster-than-light travel by then.

  • We might even have things that are considered physically impossible by the scientists of today, such as backwards time travel.

But aside from that, the sheer amount of technological development that will have taken place by then means that even if everything I've written about here becomes available, it'll be a drop in the ocean of other advances. The sheer amount of technological and social change that will have taken place by then (assuming humanity keeps progressing and doesn't suffer some catastrophe) mean that the world of 3000 will be unimaginable to someone from this era.
